title: Homelessness payments to nonprofits per person who left homelessness for permanent housing
question: How much did the homelessness department pay nonprofits for each person recorded as leaving homelessness for permanent housing?
finding: Per exit to permanent housing, State count: $76,258 in 2020 and $126,109 in 2025 (+65%), as the money went from $181.5 million to $489.4 million (+170%) and the count from 2,380 to 3,881 (+63%). Per exit to permanent housing, City count: $67,747 in 2023 and $97,322 in 2025 (+44%), as the money went from $361.1 million to $489.4 million (+36%) and the count from 5,330 to 5,029 (-6%).
how: Money: all payments by the Department of Homelessness and Supportive Housing to nonprofits in the City fiscal year ending in June of the year shown. State count: people who exited homelessness into permanent housing in that calendar year, as computed by the State from the homelessness data system (the State's measure 3). City count: the homelessness department's own yearly figure for people exiting homelessness to permanent housing, published since fiscal year 2023. The two counts use different rules and periods and are shown as separate lines.
limits: The State counts calendar years and the City fiscal years, so the money and the State count overlap by six months only. The money is everything the department paid nonprofits that year, so this is the cost of the whole system set against one result, not the price of that result: most of the money keeps people housed, sheltered or in care who are not counted as a new result. A falling count can reflect harder cases or fewer openings rather than weaker work, and the pandemic distorted 2020 to 2022.
